device: Coral USB Accelerator (Google Inc. 18d1:9302), single inference
produced_by: src/etpu/runtime/bench.py, 15 warmup + 100 timed invoke() per model
what: What a 30% parameter cut buys on the CLIP RN50 image tower, measured. Both rows are per-channel int8 -- the granularity this family pins, and the only one whose zero-shot survives (results/clip_rn50/zero_shot.json).

rows.zero_shot_top1_measured_on: onnx2tf build; NOT re-evaluated on the litert build
onnx2tf build; NOT re-evaluated on the litert build

finding: A 30.3% cut in file size (37.34 -> 26.02 MiB) removes 48.5% of the streamed weights (16.09 -> 8.29 MiB) and 38.4% of the latency (51.51 -> 31.75 ms, 1.62x). The on-chip share barely moves (6.60 -> 6.70 MiB) and the mapping does not move at all (107 operations, 79 on the TPU and 28 on the CPU, one subgraph, both rows). Everything pruning bought here it bought by not streaming bytes.
corrects: families/classification/clip_rn50/README.md quoted 36.6 -> 26.0 MiB and off-chip 15.9 -> 8.3 MiB. Those pairs mixed quantisation granularities: 36.6351 MiB and the 15.9 figure come from the PER-TENSOR build (outputs/edgetpu/single_20260623_151848/, 15:18), while 26.02 comes from the PER-CHANNEL pruned build (single_20260623_162222/, 16:22). The per-tensor build is the one whose zero-shot collapses to 18.83%, so it is not a configuration this family would ship, and its size is not the right 'before'. Same-granularity throughout, the pair is 37.34 -> 26.02 MiB and 16.09 -> 8.29 MiB. The thesis is unaffected; the numbers were.
latency_law_note: This repo's line_seg-fitted law (2.260*offchip + 0.917*onchip + 0.861) predicts 43.3 and 25.7 ms against 51.5 and 31.8 measured -- under by 1.19x and 1.23x. Expected: 28 of the 107 operations run on the CPU here, and a weight-transfer law has no term for them. The DIFFERENCE transfers better than the levels: the law predicts a 17.6 ms saving from the 7.80 MiB of streaming removed, against 19.8 ms measured.
cpu_ops_caveat: The 28 CPU operations are the attention-pooling head (BATCH_MATMUL, SOFTMAX, GATHER, TRANSPOSE, FULLY_CONNECTED and the reshapes around them). The measured milliseconds include them, because they are inside the same interpreter invoke(). This is not a fully-mapped model like the EfficientDet ladder.

export_path_migration.what: Both models re-converted through litert-torch + ai-edge-quantizer, re-compiled and re-benched on the same Coral. The *_onnx2tf fields on each row keep the previous path's values.
export_path_migration.headline: The AttentionPool2d head does NOT map on this path either. This family's README used to warn against assuming the head is intrinsically unmappable, because EfficientDet's CPU fallback turned out to be an exporter artifact. For CLIP it is not: litert-torch leaves the head on the CPU too, and slightly more of it (28 -> 33 operators). The TPU side is unchanged at 79 operators on both paths.
export_path_migration.what_blocks_it: BATCH_MATMUL x2 and SOFTMAX -- the attention itself. The Edge TPU has no batch matmul, so the QK and AV products cannot map at any shape. 6 TRANSPOSE and 1 FULLY_CONNECTED come back 'otherwise supported, but not mapped due to some unspecified limitation'; the remaining 23 are 'More than one subgraph is not supported', i.e. they cascade from the cut rather than being unmappable themselves.
export_path_migration.bytes_unchanged: on-chip 6.60 / 6.70 MiB and off-chip 16.09 / 8.29 MiB are identical to the onnx2tf build on both rows.
export_path_migration.latency_caveat: 51.506 -> 64.397 ms unpruned and 31.750 -> 40.477 ms pruned, both slower. Do NOT read these as an accelerator result. A third of this graph runs on the development host's CPU, which is not the deployment target and is not held fixed between the two dates -- exactly the confound README finding 3 describes. What IS comparable is the mapping and the byte split, and those say the head stays on the CPU.
export_path_migration.accuracy: zero_shot_top1 NOT re-measured; the committed figures are from the onnx2tf build. Weight granularity is per-channel on both paths, which is the setting this family collapses without.
